speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with your history: Have you had any recent infections, kidney stones, or trauma to your right side? Also, is the pain severe enough to cause nausea or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any pain during urination, and has the blood in your urine appeared in episodes or constantly? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance - Reddish, WBC - 10-20 /HPF, RBC - Too numerous to count, Nitrites - Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase - Positive

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the flank pain ever radiated to your groin or testicle, and have you noticed any gravel-like particles in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Non-contrast CT KUB.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ureteral Colic secondary to a small ureteral stone (likely passed or radiolucent).
